title: The SOLID principles
idea: SOLID is five rules for classes that keep change cheap: one reason to change, extend without editing, honest subtypes, small interfaces, and depending on abstractions.

analogy.text: A kitchen with standard sockets. Each appliance does one thing, and you plug in a new one without rewiring the wall.
analogy.breaks: Code has no physical socket; you design the interface yourself.

points: Each principle answers one question: what breaks when a requirement changes?
New behaviour should arrive as a new class, not an edit to working code.
A subclass must work anywhere its parent works, with no surprises.
High-level code depends on an abstraction; concrete helpers are passed in from outside.

hero.title: Five rules, five smells
head: Principle
Rule
Smell it fixes
rows: One reason to change per class
Invoice class that also emails and saves
Override that throws or does nothing
Classes stubbing methods they never use
hero.caption: Read each row as: if you smell this, apply that rule.

code.title: S, O, I, D together
code.caption: Add a `Cap` rule that limits the total to 50, and pass it in. `Checkout` never changes.

walk.text: Each discount is its own class with one job: S.
Both expose one method, `apply(total)`. In JS, that method shape is the interface: I.
`Checkout` depends only on the `apply` shape; concrete rules are injected: D.
It only knows `apply`, so new rules need no edit here: O.
Compose rules at the edge of the program, then run.

code.title: Breaking Liskov
code.caption: `LockedDeposit` is an `Account` by syntax, but not by behaviour. Callers pay the price.

pitfalls: Split a class only when its parts change for different reasons.
An override that throws `not supported` signals a wrong inheritance tree.
Injection helps only if the receiving class calls the method and never checks `instanceof`.

quiz.why: The first rule turns 50 into 20. The second floors 20 minus 30 at zero with `Math.max`.

takeaway: SOLID keeps change local: small jobs, honest subtypes, injected abstractions.
